title: Traffic-slice Config Oracle: randomized rollout + regression-aware rollback for batching/caching
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: build and validate a randomized traffic-slice experiment harness ("Config Oracle") that recommends and safely applies batching/caching configuration changes while automatically detecting regressions and triggering rollback. This ticket focuses on experiment design, metric definitions, dashboarding, and a deterministic rollback policy that minimizes downstream customer impact.
comments: 2026-02-28 — Kickoff: outlined objective with PM + SRE. Decided to target conservative default policies and then expand. Agreed on traffic slicing by tenant and by request path for fine-grained signals.

2026-03-01 — Implementation plan: (1) experiment runner that pushes candidate config to subset of hosts via feature flag; (2) telemetry tagging for slice_id and config_id; (3) safety gate logic in the controller that monitors metrics and reverts if thresholds breached. Diego to prototype controller; Asha to own metrics & dashboards.

2026-03-02 — Metric spec approved by SRE: primary metrics = cost-per-1k-tokens (serve_cost_per_k), request P95 latency (p95_latency_ms), error rate (5xx_rate), and quality regression signal (eval_prompt_pass_rate). Secondary: throughput (tokens/s), KV cache hit rate, prefix latency. Use sequential testing with alpha=0.01 for early stop, apply Bonferroni correction across cohorts.

2026-03-03 — Design review notes from Product: include per-customer thresholds (high-value customers have stricter rollback thresholds), and a grace window for cache warm-up (default 10 minutes). Product requested a 'degraded-quality' label for any slice that shows eval_pass_rate drop >= 2 percentage points.

Action items: (A) Create Grafana dashboard panels for per-slice baselines and deltas (Asha). (B) Add controller integration tests that simulate KV-prefetch failures and traffic surges (Diego). (C) Draft runbook for manual override and post-mortem (SRE).
experiment_design: Randomized assignment at tenant granularity with stratified buckets by traffic percentile and model family. 4-arm experiment: control, lightweight-batching (minibatch=4), aggressive-batching (minibatch=16), prefetched-cache (prefix_kv_enabled=true). Rolling windows: 30m warm-up + 60m observation. Canary expansion policy requires: no P95 regression > 15% and cost improvement >= 8% vs control in the observation window.
safety_and_rollback_policy: Controller monitors trailing windows (5/30/60-min). Immediate rollback triggers: p95_latency increase > 25% OR 5xx_rate increase > 0.5 percentage points OR eval_prompt_pass_rate drop > 2 percentage points for customer-slice flagged as high-value. Soft rollback (reduce aggressiveness) if KV hit-rate drops by >10% but no quality regressions. All rollbacks logged with audit-id and linked to PR that applied change.
metrics_to_track: serve_cost_per_k, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, 99_latency_ms, 5xx_rate, eval_prompt_pass_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, tokens_per_request, throughput_tokens_s, rollbacks_count, time_to_rollback_minutes
analysis_plan: Compute relative deltas vs control per slice with bootstrapped CIs. Use sequential stopping (alpha=0.01) and require at least 5000 requests per slice for decision. For quality metrics, tie to eval prompt set and compute per-prompt failure counts; apply hierarchical shrinkage across tenants to stabilize estimates.
dashboard_notes: Grafana panels: slice map (traffic by tenant), cost delta heatmap, latency distribution overlay, quality regression timeline, rollback events annotation layer. Add Alerting: fire PagerDuty if any high-value slice enters immediate rollback criteria. Add CSV export for ad-hoc analysis.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: small tenants produce noisy signals -> mitigate with minimum-traffic floor and hierarchical modeling. Risk: long-tail interactions between batching and function-calling -> mitigate by including synthetic test cases that exercise tool-calls in the controller tests. Operational risk: cascading rollbacks when many slices fail simultaneously -> implement staggered rollback and capacity circuit breaker.
next_steps: 1) Merge controller prototype PR and run closed traffic replay (assigned Diego). 2) Stand up Grafana staging dashboard and link experiment tags (Asha). 3) Run 2-week canary on internal customers (beta tenants) then expand cohort. 4) Prepare PRD for gradated product rollout if results stable.
notes_for_reviewers: When reviewing, focus on (a) metric definitions and thresholds, (b) controller test coverage for failure modes, and (c) dashboard panels required for fast triage. Prefer concrete threshold numbers over vague guidance so SRE can automate rollbacks.
audit_trail_policy: Every automated apply/rollback must emit an audit event to the control-plane event stream with fields (slice_id, config_id, reason, metrics_snapshot). Events stored for 90 days by default and retained 365 days for enterprise customers (tunable).
